knowledge_gaps: Relative-position bias is a reasonable first experiment, but calling it the best option is unsupported by comparative evidence. Originality 3/10 is reasonable; potential 7/10 is speculative, and difficulty 4/10 depends on the supplied attention implementation.

The report omits direct prior art on bucketed relative-attention bias, particularly T5, and relative-position/time-aware sequential recommendation such as TiSASRec. TemProxRec alone does not establish novelty or the implementation rationale.

Reproducibility requires the actual baseline configuration, attention integration, optimizer parameter registration, bias regularization policy, checkpoint cadence, and numerical parity tolerances. Constructing nn.Embedding consumes random numbers before zero initialization, so seed 42 alone does not ensure identical backbone initialization or subsequent sampling across controls.

Zero bias should reproduce baseline outputs before training, but this needs an explicit check. The expanded B×H×L×L floating mask may change attention kernel selection, memory use, and runtime; the claim of little computational overhead is unverified under the shared GPU budget.

The evaluation plan lacks prespecified uncertainty reporting and controls for repeated validation selection. Margins should distinguish terminal from interior targets. Learned position preferences can exploit recency or sequence-length shortcuts and need not resolve broad semantic matches; frozen recent-versus-older context interventions would provide supporting evidence without changing the selection metric.
